component.name: Eclipse
component.summary: Run the Android Roblox client on Linux

description.p: Eclipse is an open-source runtime, written in Rust, that runs the official and unmodified Android Roblox client on Linux with native Vulkan graphics, audio, and keyboard and mouse input.

Eclipse does not include or redistribute Roblox. On first launch it downloads Roblox's own release files and installs them only when Roblox Corporation's signature verifies, then keeps the client updated. It can also install official APK files from your Downloads folder.

screenshot.caption: The launch window downloading the official Roblox client

ul.li: Security fixes: Roblox's signature is checked before its files are read, eclipse run with a file path plays a private verified copy, game output shown in a terminal can no longer send control sequences, and WebView bridge calls are bounded.
Less memory and work at launch: Roblox's resource tables are read once from a memory map, and in-memory code loads no longer run dex2oat on every launch.
Ctrl+C on eclipse run stops Roblox and cleans up.
Groundwork for 64-bit ARM Linux. ARM builds are not published yet.
Roblox sees the real window size, and its interface follows the display scale on HiDPI monitors.
The run log says which microphone Roblox records from and whether it hears sound.
When the GPU driver loses the graphics device, for example after suspend, Eclipse says so, and on NVIDIA how to keep video memory across suspend.
eclipse shortcut adds a game to the app menu.
Fixed an error each time the game window went fullscreen, and a crash when a software-rendered window closed.
Roblox can decode H.264, HEVC and AAC media for videos in experiences, through the runtime's FFmpeg. eclipse doctor lists the decoders and says how to add H.264 and HEVC when they are missing.
Game audio opens at 48 kHz stereo whenever the device offers it.
Eclipse counts audio underruns and logs them.
Desktop volume mixers show the game's audio as Eclipse, with its icon.
Eclipse updates Roblox again, from APKPure, or from Google Play after a one-time play-login.
Roblox sees a microphone, as on a phone.
Roblox's "Roblox Upgrade" dialog no longer fails with a missing layout.
Security fixes: a TLS update for four RustSec advisories, stricter parsing of Roblox's files, a private app-data folder and cookie flood protection for the Roblox login.
Roblox's libraries and fonts are memory-mapped instead of read into memory.
Roblox 2.742 starts. Roblox no longer lets 2.741 join games, so install 2.742 with Install from files or eclipse install.
A hidden or minimized Roblox draws at most 5 frames a second, and unfocused_fps_limit caps it while another window has focus.
Opening Eclipse again while it runs no longer fails with "did not answer".
Eclipse Settings can send Roblox's sound and microphone to a chosen device, such as a USB microphone, without changing your desktop defaults.
Roblox renders on the GPU you choose with vulkan_device, and on hybrid laptops it sees only that GPU. use_opengl switches to OpenGL ES, which is also picked automatically when no Vulkan GPU works.
eclipse doctor names the GPU and driver problems it finds and how to fix them.
Closing one of Roblox's own small windows, such as the purchase "Working…" box, no longer resizes the game or crashes Roblox.
Eclipse Settings, from the app menu or eclipse settings, sets controls, updates and performance, and copies a bug report or opens the log folder.
eclipse doctor checks the setup, and the failure window leads with the cause and how to fix it.
Joining an experience with voice chat no longer crashes Roblox.
When Roblox crashes, Eclipse closes completely, and its error window closes with Escape, Enter or its Close button.
Choosing a Robux package now reaches Roblox, which explains that purchases need Google Play. Buy Robux on roblox.com instead; it uses the same account.
Controllers work through SDL3, touchscreens send real multi-finger touches, and touchpad scrolling no longer depends on your display scale.
Eclipse remembers its window size and fullscreen state, closes cleanly when Roblox exits, and can show the server's location or close when you leave a game.
Roblox is ready about twice as fast after an update. eclipse rollback returns to the previous version, and eclipse storage shows and cleans what Eclipse keeps on disk.
On Wayland, Buy Robux, sign-in and other Roblox web pages now open inside the game window: they move with it and cannot be dragged off it. X11 keeps a separate window.
Links and shares from Roblox open through your desktop, Roblox notifications show on it, and the screen stays awake while you play. GameMode is used when it is installed.
Steam's on-screen keyboard opens when you select a text box while Steam runs.
Buy Robux and other Roblox web pages now cover the game window exactly, and move with it when it is resized.
More kinds of Roblox links open in Eclipse, and starting Eclipse while Roblox runs asks the desktop to show the running game instead of reporting an error.
Roblox captures are saved in Pictures/Roblox, voice chat can use the microphone, and each launch keeps its own log; the last five are kept.

Sign-in and other Roblox web pages open as a dialog over the game; the game ignores your keys and clicks until the page closes. Escape or the close button closes the page, and the mouse's back button goes back.
After a resize or a switch to fullscreen, Eclipse keeps offering the game the new window size until it takes it, so the game no longer stays drawn at the old size.

description.p: Sign-in and other Roblox web pages now open in a WebKitGTK window from the GNOME runtime instead of a bundled Chromium, so Eclipse takes under 100 MB instead of more than 450 MB. Your login carries over once from the old web engine; if it cannot, the log says why, and you sign in again.

ul.li: A mistake in config.json no longer stops Eclipse: that setting keeps its default, and the launch window and eclipse config name the problem.
Eclipse's log keeps only the site of each web address, so it carries no sign-in links.
Text boxes edit correctly with input methods and right-to-left text, the client gets your time zone, and its Android resources match your language.
The game keeps drawing when a monitor is connected or removed, and sound no longer stays silent after the sound server fails a stream.
Launches no longer hang on a clipboard that never answers or a window that never appears, and a Roblox update removes the files the new version dropped.

description.p: When APKCombo has no x86-64 build of the newest Roblox release yet, Eclipse installs the newest release that has one instead of failing.

ul.li: A launch window shows the update check, the download and any error until Roblox opens. Downloads resume where they stopped, and only one Roblox client runs at a time.
Roblox's Maximum Frame Rate setting appears, with limits up to 240 FPS, and the client sees your monitor's refresh rates.
Text boxes work with input methods, the desktop clipboard and the usual editing keys, F11 toggles fullscreen, and switching windows releases every held key.

description.p: The first release with a Flatpak. The 0.1.0 Flatpak build failed while unpacking the web engine for sign-in pages, and this release fixes it.

The first release. Eclipse downloads the official Android Roblox client without an account, installs it only when Roblox's signature verifies, and runs it with Vulkan graphics, audio, and keyboard and mouse input.
The Play button on the Roblox website opens games in Eclipse through roblox:// and roblox-player: links.
